## Generate Batch RMA Results

This document is for creating a batch of files to input into RMAPLT to create rasters of depth for each timepoint, and then running each file in RMAPLT to generate rasters, reading back in rasters, converting them to binary (wet/dry) rasters, and summing these rasters to calculate how long each cell is inundated, and therefore total residence times.

### 1. Set up

Before we start, load packages.

```{r Packages}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(terra)
library(sf)
```

Then, load in the text file we're going to edit to create batch files.

```{r Txt_file}
txt82 <- readLines("C:/Users/z5204897/OneDrive - UNSW/Desktop/RMA/BlueHeart/runs/BH023_0082/runbatch/run0082_runbatchresults.txt")

# these are the lines we'll be modifying
txt82[4]
txt82[6]
```

### 2. Generate RMAPLT results for each time point

Next, create a loop to create modified versions of this file for every value from 1628-4318. Store them in a list (seq_list).

```{r modify_txt}
## insert list of desired time steps here
timesteps <- c(1628:4318)
## insert number 1 lower than earliest timestep here
preTime <- 1627
## insert model number here 
model <- "082"
## insert input file here
input <- txt82

## don't need to modify these lines
seq_list <- list()
for(i in seq_along(timesteps)){
  n <- i + preTime #timestep number to assign - starting from 1628
  seq_list[[i]] <- input
  seq_list[[i]][6] <- paste0("STEPS       ",n, "    ",n)
  seq_list[[i]][4] <- paste0("OUTASC  BH023_0", model, "_Depths_",n,".ASC")
  names(seq_list)[i] <- paste0("run", model, "_",n)
}
```

Save each item in the list as a file.

```{r Save_files}
# Define a function to save each element
save_to_file <- function(item, name) {
  filename <- paste0("C:/Users/z5204897/OneDrive - UNSW/Desktop/RMA/BlueHeart/runs/BH023_0", model, "/runbatch/", name, ".ctl")
  writeLines(item, con = filename)
}

# Apply the function across the list using mapply (which handles multiple arguments, 'item' and 'name')
mapply(save_to_file, seq_list, names(seq_list))
```

Run each file in the executable RMAPLT to create rasters.

```{r RunInExecutable}
setwd("C:/Users/z5204897/Documents/RMAoffline/runs/run0082/runbatch")

ctl_files <- list.files(path = "C:/Users/z5204897/Documents/RMAoffline/runs/run0082/runbatch", pattern = "\\.ctl$")

# Define the path to your executable
executable_path <- "C:/Users/z5204897/Documents/RMAoffline/RMAPLTV97C-july25.exe"

for (i in seq_along(ctl_files)) {
    print(paste("Processing file:", ctl_files[[i]]))

    input_path <- paste0("C:/Users/z5204897/Documents/RMAoffline/runs/run0082/runbatch/", ctl_files[[i]]) 
    
    # Execute the command
    # stdout=TRUE captures the standard output, which can be useful for debugging
    system2(command = executable_path, 
            args = input_path, 
            stdout = FALSE, 
            stderr = FALSE)
}

```

### 3. Summarise by Month and Day

After all asciis have been created, we want to create some summary stats from these:

-   convert all to binary rasters

-   summary rasters based on binary rasters:

    -   for each day - what % of time was each cell inundated

    -   for the full month - what % of time was each cell inundated

-   summary csv with total area inundated in each floodplain (+ channels) at each time point

First, convert rasters to binary rasters.

```{r BinaryRasters}
# reclassification thresholds - anything ~0 becomes 0 (not wet), >0 becomes 1 (wet)
#thresholds <- matrix(
#  c(0, 0.00001, 0,
#    0.00001, 10, 1),
#  ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

# try calling 0-2cm "dry" to account for model issues in drying.
thresholds2 <- matrix(
  c(0, 0.02, 0,
    0.02, 10, 1),
  ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)

# put files into a list
ascii_files <- list.files(path = "C:/Users/z5204897/Documents/RMAoffline/runs/run0082/runbatch", pattern = "\\.ASC$", full.names = TRUE)

ascii_names <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(ascii_files))

# make sure R reads these as rasters not just file names
raster_list <- lapply(ascii_files, terra::rast)
names(raster_list) <- ascii_names

# make a new empty list for binary rasters
#binary_rasters <- list()

binary_rasters2 <- list()

# loop creating binary rasters
#for (i in seq_along(raster_list)) {
#    print(paste("Processing file:", raster_list[[i]]))
#
#    binary_rasters[[i]] <- classify(raster_list[[i]], thresholds, include.lowest = #TRUE)
#}

for (i in seq_along(raster_list)) {
    print(paste("Processing file:", raster_list[[i]]))

    binary_rasters2[[i]] <- classify(raster_list[[i]], thresholds2, include.lowest = TRUE)
}
```

Next, create a raster stack of all rasters so we can perform calculations on it.

-   sum month

```{r RasterCalcs}

rasterStack <- rast(binary_rasters2)

sumMonth <- app(rasterStack, fun = sum, na.rm = TRUE)

#writeRaster(sumMonth, here(paste0("Output/raster/run0", model, "/sumMonth2.tif")), overwrite = TRUE)
# don't write next, leave to manipulate and write the % inundation raster instead
```

Also sum by day. For this, we'll need to load in data to understand which time step corresponds to which day/hour etc.

```{r SumByDay}
# this is the raw itr results file, trimmed to the timesteps we're using here. 
itr <- read.csv("C:/Users/z5204897/OneDrive - UNSW/Desktop/RMA/BlueHeart/runs/BH023_0082/BH023_0082_1628-4318.csv")

#There are many lines per time step and spaces of rows and we want to delete all these.

TimeStepLookup <- na.omit(itr) %>% # remove empty rows
  select(c(X17, X0.25, X1628, X1)) %>%  # only select relevant columns
  filter(X1 == 2) %>%  # only select the second iteration of each timestep (as the first iteration of the first timestep was transformed into column names here, and we just need one row per time step) 
  select(c(X17, X0.25, X1628)) %>% # now we don't need that last col anymore
  rename(Day = X17, # rename all columns so they are logical
         Hour = X0.25, 
         Timestep = X1628)

# summarise this table to determine the first and last timestep in each Day
TimeStepByDay <- TimeStepLookup %>% group_by(Day) %>% reframe(min = as.numeric(min(Timestep)), max = as.numeric(max(Timestep))) %>%  
  mutate(difference = max - min + 1) %>% # this is the number of steps in that day
  mutate(differencePlus1 = max - 1628 + 1)  # this is the raster number in the list of rasters at which to stop at for that day
TimeStepByDay

# now in the list of rasters, we can select by day using min and max
for (i in 1:29) {
    print(paste("Processing day:", i+16))

    assign(paste0("run0",model,"_Day",i + 16), binary_rasters2[(TimeStepByDay$min[i]-1627) : (TimeStepByDay$max[i]-1627)])
}

# make a list of all days
DayNames <- ls(pattern = paste0("^","run0",model,"_Day"))
# now actually retrive the objects into this list
DayObjects <- mget(DayNames)



# 1. Option if you want to save absolute values of number of inundation time points. (less recommended)
# stack these rasters, sum per day and write them as tiffs.

for (i in 1:28) {
    print(paste("Processing day:", i+16))

    rasterStack <- rast(unlist(DayObjects[i]))
    
    sumDay <- app(rasterStack, fun = sum, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    writeRaster(sumDay, here(paste0("Output/raster/run0", model, "/sumDay", i+16, ".tif")), overwrite = TRUE)
}

# 2. Option if you don't want to save absolute values and keep them as objects in R for now, just generate tiffs at the next stage (inundation %) (recommended)
sumDay <- list()

for (i in 1:28) {
    print(paste("Processing day:", i+16))

    rasterStack <- rast(unlist(DayObjects[i]))
    
    sumDay[[i]] <- app(rasterStack, fun = sum, na.rm = TRUE)
}

```

Turn each of the day rasters into % time points inundated rather than absolute values which don't mean much.

```{r %inun}
# 1. option if you saved (wrote output) raster files above (less recommended)
workingdir <- here(paste0("Output/raster/run0", model))

absolute_files <- list.files(path = workingdir, pattern = c("\\.tif"), full.names = TRUE)
# next time, don't make the files yet and just read in the list of working files, then create rasters only after % inundation calculations

raster_names <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(absolute_files))

# make sure R reads these as rasters not just file names
raster_abs <- lapply(absolute_files, terra::rast)
names(raster_abs) <- raster_names


## 2. ALTERNATIVE IF YOU HAVEN'T SAVED FILES ABOVE (recommended)
raster_abs <- append(sumDay, list(sumMonth)) # just add the month raster to the list of Days

# 3. proceed as normal here either scenario
percent_files <- list() # create an empty list in which to store transformed rasters

for (i in seq_along(raster_abs)) {
    print(paste("Processing file:", raster_abs[[i]]))
  
    max_value <- global(raster_abs[[i]], fun = "max", na.rm = TRUE) # determine max value in raster

    percent_files[[i]] <- raster_abs[[i]]/max_value[[1,1]]
    
    writeRaster(percent_files[[i]], here(paste0("Output/raster/inun_", names(raster_abs)[i], ".tif")), overwrite = TRUE)
}

```

### 4. Summarise by area (csv)

Also, create a summary csv that lists the area inundated in each floodplain wetland or in channels at each time point.

To do this, we need a shapefile with our areas.

```{r Summary csv}
blueheartareas <- st_read("C:/Users/z5204897/OneDrive - UNSW/Desktop/PhD/Spatial/Data/shp/Blue_Heart_Sites/Blue_Heart_Sites_Hydrodynamics.shp")

blueheartareas$Name
```

Subset this shapefile for only areas relevant to the present scenario:

1.  2A1
2.  2A3
3.  5B
4.  5C
5.  1D
6.  3A (YCW)
7.  5a
8.  1C
9.  3B
10. 5D
11. 2A2
12. 1A
13. 2B
14. 1B
15. Natural North
16. Natural South
17. Yandina Creek
18. Coolum Creek

![](images/clipboard-723623445.png)

```{r subset_shp_clip_raster}
relevant_nos <- c(6,15,16,17,18) # substitute whichever areas are relevant to the present scenario
blueheartrelevant <- blueheartareas[relevant_nos,]

# check that shapefile and raster line up - if so, they have compatible coordinate systems
plot(binary_rasters2[[1]])
plot(blueheartrelevant, add = TRUE)

# summarise the area inundated per wetland (+ channels= areas not captured in polygons, but have water) at each time point - test for 1 time point
sum_per_polygon <- terra::extract(x = binary_rasters2[[1]], y = blueheartrelevant, fun = sum, na.rm = TRUE) # calculate area inundated per polygon
sum_not_polygons <- global(binary_rasters2[[1]], fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]] - sum(sum_per_polygon$BH023_0082_DEPTHS_1628) # calculate area inundated not in polygons
sum_per_polygon_longer <- sum_per_polygon %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = -ID,
    names_to = "TimeStep",
    values_to = "Inundation",) # transform polygon dataframe longer first
sum_per_polygon_wider <- sum_per_polygon_longer %>% pivot_wider(names_from = ID, values_from = Inundation) %>% # then transform wider so that we end up with one row per timestep
  rename("YCW" = "1", "NaturalNorth" = "2", "NaturalSouth" = "3", "Yandina Creek" =  "4", "Coolum Creek" = "5") %>%  # rename columns for interpretability
  mutate(Other = sum_not_polygons)




# do this as a loop
summary_tibble <- filter(sum_per_polygon_wider, FALSE) # first create an empty tibble with the correct structure


for(i in seq_along(binary_rasters2)){
  print(paste("Processing file:", binary_rasters2[[i]]))

  sum_per_polygon <- terra::extract(x = binary_rasters2[[i]], y = blueheartrelevant, fun = sum, na.rm = TRUE) # calculate area inundated per polygon
  sum_not_polygons <- global(binary_rasters2[[i]], fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]] - sum(sum_per_polygon[2]) # calculate area inundated not in polygons
  sum_per_polygon_longer <- sum_per_polygon %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = -ID,
    names_to = "TimeStep",
    values_to = "Inundation",) # transform polygon dataframe longer first
  sum_per_polygon_wider <- sum_per_polygon_longer %>% pivot_wider(names_from = ID, values_from = Inundation) %>% # then transform wider so that we end up with one row per timestep
  rename("YCW" = "1", "NaturalNorth" = "2", "NaturalSouth" = "3", "Yandina Creek" =  "4", "Coolum Creek" = "5") %>%  # rename columns for interpretability
  mutate(Other = sum_not_polygons)

  summary_tibble <- summary_tibble %>% add_row(sum_per_polygon_wider[1,])
}

summary_tibble2 <- summary_tibble %>% 
  rename(Timestep = TimeStep) %>% 
  mutate(Timestep = substr(Timestep,19,22)) %>% 
  full_join(TimeStepLookup)



# these are numbers of grid cells inundated, let's also get total area in each section for % inundation
extracted_values <- extract(binary_rasters2[[1]], blueheartrelevant)

# The 'table' function groups and counts the occurrences of each ID
cell_counts <- table(extracted_values$ID) 

# View the result: ID (polygon ID) and Freq (cell count)
print(cell_counts)

cell_counts[1]


summary_tibble3 <- summary_tibble2 %>% select(-c("Yandina Creek", "Coolum Creek", "Other")) %>% 
  mutate(YCW_percent = YCW / cell_counts[1] * 100,
         NaturalNorth_percent = NaturalNorth / cell_counts[2] * 100,
         NaturalSouth_percent = NaturalSouth / cell_counts[3] * 100,
         YCW_area_m2 = YCW*400,
         NaturalNorth_area_m2 = NaturalNorth*400,
         NaturalSouth_area_m2 = NaturalSouth*400)


write.csv(summary_tibble3, here(paste0("Output/csv/run0",model,"_summary.csv")))

```
